key_insight: A reverse-diode element explains inefficient electron extraction and S-shaped current–voltage behavior in valley photovoltaic devices.
engineering_relevance: Eliminating the reverse-diode bottleneck is necessary for valley photovoltaic devices to achieve high efficiency.
method: Measure intensity- and voltage-dependent photoluminescence and electrical responses.
Model both responses with a shared equivalent circuit.
Use Poisson/drift-diffusion simulations to investigate the reverse diode’s origin.
evidence_signal: The equivalent-circuit model captures the measured S-shaped current–voltage curves while simultaneously describing photoluminescence and electrical measurements.
watch_item: The reverse diode could arise from valley scattering or a heterojunction barrier, so its physical origin remains unresolved.
paper_title: Combined photoluminescence and electrical characterization of valley photovoltaic devices explained with an equivalent circuit
